mainTopic: The מחלוקת between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש about proving a deed in the בני ברק case, and the age from which an heir may sell his father's property
overview: The גמרא first explains what רבי יוחנן meant when he challenged ריש לקיש. רבי יוחנן holds that proof comes from ratifying the deed (קיום השטר), while ריש לקיש requires witnesses. רבי יוחנן asks how, in ריש לקיש's view, the buyers in the בני ברק case could ever have held the land. ריש לקיש answers that a family's claim that the seller was a קטן is weak, because there is a חזקה that witnesses sign a deed only for an adult. The גמרא then brings a dispute about the age from which a young heir may sell his father's property. Both reports are in the name of רב נחמן: רבא reports 18, and רב הונא בר חיננא reports 20. The גמרא notes that רבא's report was only inferred, not said outright. Finally, רבי זירא challenges this from the בני ברק case, where רבי עקיבא would not allow the dead seller's body to be examined. He begins by showing that the case fits the 18 view, and his challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's challenge from the בני ברק case
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says to ריש לקיש: in my view, buyers can hold the land by ratifying the deed. In your view, which needs witnesses, how could the buyers ever hold it?
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what רבי יוחנן said to ריש לקיש: It works well for me. I say proof comes from ratifying the deed, so we can understand how the buyers came to hold the property. But you say proof must come from witnesses. How can the buyers ever end up holding the property?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is explaining what רבי יוחנן really meant when he challenged ריש לקיש. He uses the בני ברק case, where the buyers were holding the land and the family was trying to take it from them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the בני ברק case the relatives were the ones contesting, so the buyers must have been in possession. Under רבי יוחנן, a ratified deed is enough to put the buyers there. Under ריש לקיש, who demands witnesses, it is hard to see how the buyers could be holding the land at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Ratifying a deed by confirming the signatures of its witnesses
They go down into the property, meaning they take possession of it
It works well (for one view). It opens a contrast: this view is fine, but the other has a problem.

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי קָאָמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ:
phrases.english: This is what Rabbi Yochanan said to Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish:
It works well according to me, since I say:
proof is by ratifying the deed —
that is how you can find a case
where the buyers take possession of the property.
But according to you, who say proof is by witnesses,
how can you find a case
where the buyers take possession of the property?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies a challenge that רבי יוחנן raised earlier on the daf
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's view that proof must come through witnesses
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the בני ברק case the buyers held the land. Under ריש לקיש's demand for witnesses, there seems to be no way they could have come to hold it.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: a family's claim that the seller was a minor is weak
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש agrees that when the family says the seller was a minor, their claim does not count. Witnesses are presumed to sign only for an adult.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said to him: I agree with you about a protest by family members, that it is not a real protest. What are they saying? That he was a minor. But there is a חזקה that witnesses do not sign a deed unless the seller had become an adult.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש answers רבי יוחנן. He explains that in the בני ברק case, the buyers can hold the land because of a special חזקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The family only claims the seller was a minor. A signed deed already carries a חזקה that the witnesses checked that he was an adult, so the deed beats the family's claim. In ריש לקיש's own case, a sick person's gift, there is no such חזקה, so witnesses are still needed.

keyTerms.meaning: A protest or challenge against someone's claim to property
Family members (here, the relatives of the dead seller)
A legal presumption that we rely on unless it is disproven

phrases.english: He said to him: I agree with you

phrases.aramaic: בְּעַרְעָר דִּבְנֵי מִשְׁפָּחָה, דְּלָאו עַרְעָר הוּא.
phrases.english: about a protest by family members, that it is not a real protest.
What are they saying? "He was a minor";

phrases.aramaic: חֲזָקָה אֵין הָעֵדִים חוֹתְמִין עַל הַשְּׁטָר,
phrases.english: there is a presumption that witnesses do not sign on a deed
unless he had become an adult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יוחנן's challenge in step 1
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: the בני ברק case has a חזקה that supports the deed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Under ריש לקיש, buyers could never hold the land without witnesses
steps.terutzMaskana: When the only claim is that the seller was a minor, the חזקה that witnesses sign only for adults lets the buyers keep the land. A sick person's gift has no such חזקה.
steps.whatToRemember: Witnesses are presumed to sign a deed only for an adult. So the claim "he was a minor" cannot cancel a signed deed.

steps.title: From what age may a young heir sell his father's property?
steps.stepSummary: Two reports of רב נחמן's view: רבא quotes him as saying 18, and רב הונא בר חיננא quotes him as saying 20.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: from when may a קטן sell his father's property? רבא said in the name of רב נחמן: from eighteen years old. רב הונא בר חיננא said in the name of רב נחמן: from twenty years old.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic connected to the בני ברק case. It asks at what age an heir may sell land he inherited from his father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here "קטן" means someone too young to sell inherited land, even if he is past בר מצוה. Both opinions come from רב נחמן. They are two different reports of what he said: 18 or 20.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated. It introduces a dispute among אמוראים.

steps.confusionAlert: Here קטן does not mean a child under בר מצוה. It means a young heir who is not yet old enough (18 or 20) to sell inherited land.

phrases.aramaic: אִיתְּמַר: קָטָן, מֵאֵימָתַי מוֹכֵר בְּנִכְסֵי אָבִיו?
phrases.english: It was stated: a minor, from when may he sell his father's property?

phrases.aramaic: רָבָא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: בֶּן שְׁמֹנֶה עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה,
phrases.english: Rava said that Rav Nachman said: from eighteen years old,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב הוּנָא בַּר חִינָּנָא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: and Rav Huna bar Chinnana said that Rav Nachman said:
from twenty years old.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר: קָטָן, מֵאֵימָתַי מוֹכֵר בְּנִכְסֵי אָבִיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic related to the בני ברק case
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are two reports of רב נחמן's view on when a young heir may sell inherited property: 18 (רבא) or 20 (רב הונא בר חיננא).

steps.title: רבא's report was only inferred
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that רבא's report of 18 was not said outright by רב נחמן. It was worked out by inference.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this report of רבא was not stated outright. Rather, it was stated by inference.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a note about how strong רבא's report is. רב נחמן never said "18" in words; it was worked out by inference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא is telling us how רבא's report came about. רב נחמן never said "18" outright; the number 18 was drawn as a conclusion from something else. רב הונא בר חיננא's "20" is not described this way.

keyTerms.meaning: By inference, worked out from something else

phrases.english: And this statement of Rava was not stated explicitly,
rather, it was stated by inference.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Qualifies the source of רבא's version in step 3
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבא's report of 18 was inferred, not stated outright by רב נחמן.

steps.title: רבי זירא brings the בני ברק case
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא quotes the בני ברק case. A man sold his father's property and died, and the family said he had been a קטן. רבי עקיבא would not allow the body to be examined, for two reasons.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא raised an objection. There was a case in בני ברק of a man who sold his father's property and then died. The family members came and protested, saying he was a minor when he died. They asked רבי עקיבא whether they could examine the body. He told them: you may not disgrace him. And besides, the signs of adulthood tend to change after death.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא is setting up a challenge to one of the age opinions. He first quotes the full story of the בני ברק case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא gives two reasons not to examine the body. First, it would disgrace the dead man. Second, it would not prove anything anyway, because the body's signs of adulthood change after death. רבי זירא will use this story to test the 18 and 20 opinions.

keyTerms.meaning: Raises an objection, usually from an earlier source

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira raised an objection:
There was an incident in Bnei Brak
involving one who sold his father's property, and died;
and family members came and protested, saying:
He was a minor at the time of his death.

phrases.aramaic: וּבָאוּ וְשָׁאֲלוּ אֶת רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: מַהוּ לְבוֹדְקוֹ?
phrases.english: And they came and asked Rabbi Akiva: May we examine him?
phrases.notes: They mean taking out the body to check for signs of adulthood.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶם: אִי אַתֶּם רַשָּׁאִין לְנַוְּולוֹ.
phrases.english: He said to them: You are not permitted to disgrace him.

phrases.aramaic: וְעוֹד, סִימָנִין עֲשׂוּיִין לְהִשְׁתַּנּוֹת לְאַחַר מִיתָה.
phrases.english: And furthermore, signs tend to change after death.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to test the age dispute in step 3
steps.kashyaTarget: One of the age opinions (18 or 20) in step 3
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Set up here by quoting the case. The actual reasoning begins in step 6.

steps.title: רבי זירא begins: it works for the view of eighteen
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא starts his reasoning. The בני ברק case fits the view that the age is 18. The challenge to the other view continues in the next part of the daf.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well according to the one who says eighteen years old...
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא begins to explain his challenge. He says the story fits the 18 opinion; the problem for the other opinion comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a "בשלמא" setup: first he shows which view fits the story. The rest of the sentence, which shows the difficulty for the 20 opinion, continues in the next part of the daf.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the one who says

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר בֶּן שְׁמֹנֶה עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה,
phrases.english: Granted, according to the one who says eighteen years old,

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר בֶּן שְׁמֹנֶה עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the reasoning of רבי זירא's objection from step 5
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that an heir may sell only from age 20
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The case fits the 18 view. The difficulty for the 20 view is spelled out in the continuation.
